Keeping peptides cool in Scottsdale

NOAA's station at Scottsdale Municipal Airport, about 1,473 feet above sea level and roughly 5 miles southwest of the city's Census center point, sets the local baseline.67 Its 1991 to 2020 normals, built on about 16 to 18 years of records, put the July normal high at 104.1 °F and the July normal low at 82.6 °F.6 The station averages 92.9 days a year at or above 100 °F and 161.4 at or above 90 °F, with 2.9 nights at or below freezing and 8.73 inches of precipitation a year.2

That is slightly milder than Phoenix Sky Harbor, whose July normal high runs 2.4 °F hotter and whose January normal low runs 2.6 °F warmer.68 Elevation makes the bigger difference inside the city, which climbs from 1,150 to 4,877 feet.1 NOAA's Pinnacle Peak station, at about 2,565 feet in north Scottsdale, averages a July high of 99.4 °F and a July low of 75.9 °F.3

Light deserves the same care as heat. GenScript, a peptide maker, advises keeping freeze-dried peptides at -20 °C away from bright light, and notes that stability varies with each peptide's sequence.5 FDA labels for approved freeze-dried tesamorelin and somatropin products say to keep the vials in the original box or carton to protect them from light.91011 For a research vial, the practical version is a closed box, away from light, at the temperature its label or product page gives. The storage guide covers the details.

About Scottsdale

Scottsdale incorporated in 1951 and still calls itself "The West's Most Western Town".1 It runs from the Salt River in the south to the Tonto National Forest in the north, with the McDowell Mountains on its eastern side.1 The Census Bureau estimates 243,006 residents on July 1, 2025, on 184.0 square miles of land.127 Survey data describe an older, highly educated city: a median age of 47.7, 28.0 percent of residents aged 65 or older, and 64.3 percent of adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree or higher (2024 American Community Survey).131415

By the city's count, Old Town Scottsdale has more than 90 restaurants, 320 retail shops and more than 80 art galleries.1 The McDowell Sonoran Preserve protects nearly 48 square miles of Sonoran Desert, and the city's list of top attractions includes Taliesin West, McCormick-Stillman Railroad Park, the Indian Bend Wash Greenbelt and Scottsdale Fashion Square.16 The city counts more than 31,000 companies and 220,000 jobs, with healthcare and finance firms leading its list of top employers.1617

Mayo Clinic's Scottsdale location is a teaching and research site. It houses the Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine, the Center for Procedural Skills Innovation and two research buildings, the Collaborative Research Building and the Samuel C. Johnson Research Building.18 Its Mayo Clinic Building adds outpatient surgery, laboratory space, diagnostic testing, imaging and pharmacy services.18

Nearby

The county hub is Peptides in Phoenix, the city on Scottsdale's western border.1 Mayo Clinic's Scottsdale and Phoenix locations are 14 miles apart.18 Tempe, Mesa and Fountain Hills have pages of their own, and the locations page covers all three counties.

Frequently asked questions

Do Scottsdale orders ship any differently from Phoenix orders?

No. There is no separate Scottsdale service: orders for any address in the city leave from the USA and Canada and follow the same shipping policy as Phoenix and the rest of the country. The product page shows strengths and stock before you order. For the county as a whole, including a comparison of summer heat at seven NOAA stations, see Peptides in Phoenix.

Can retatrutide be delivered to a Scottsdale address?

Yes. Retatrutide is listed in 10 mg, 30 mg vials and ships to Scottsdale like the rest of the catalog, with current stock shown on its product page. It is sold as a research material only, and its product page carries the research-use notice. For what published studies report about it, read What is Retatrutide?, and for multi-vial lab orders see Bulk retatrutide and tirzepatide research vials.

Is storage any easier in cooler north Scottsdale?

Only a little. NOAA's Pinnacle Peak station in the north of the city averages a July high of 99.4 °F and 45.3 days a year at or above 100 °F, about half the count at Scottsdale Municipal Airport.34 That is still far warmer than a freezer or fridge. GenScript, a peptide maker, recommends storing freeze-dried peptides at -20 °C, away from bright light,5 so wherever in Scottsdale a parcel lands, it goes indoors right away and each vial is stored as its label or product page directs.

Is there a D2C Peptides showroom or office in Scottsdale?

No. D2C Peptides lists no showroom, office or other location in Scottsdale or anywhere else in Maricopa County, so this page gives no street address, phone number or map. Every Scottsdale order is handled by shipping. If you need help before or after ordering, the contact page is the way to reach us.
